Featured Case Study

The Hebrew Tabernacle doors

Some doors are hardware. These are history. SHAPE's restoration of the Hebrew Tabernacle's Art Deco doors is the kind of work the studio is known for — where getting it right means respecting the original craft while making the metal perform for the next century.

Representative detail

Restoring an Art Deco entrance, panel by panel

Art Deco metalwork leaves nowhere to hide. Chevron geometry, sunburst fans, floral relief — every panel has to line up, catch light the same way, and sit true in its frame. Restoration at this level is part detective work, part fabrication.

ProjectHebrew Tabernacle — door restoration

1 · Assess & document

Condition, original finishes, and damaged details are documented before any metal is touched.

2 · Repair & replicate

Missing or failed elements are repaired or faithfully replicated to match the original relief and profile.

3 · Refinish & protect

Patina and finish are matched across old and new metal so the entrance reads as one piece — then protected for daily use.

Materials & Finishes — Interactive

Pick a finish. See the character.

Tap a finish to preview it at scale. Every finish is sampled and approved before fabrication — the photos below are representative of each finish family.

Representative finish photo

Brushed Brass

Directional grain softens reflections and fingerprints far better than polished brass. A classic for landmark entrances — and the natural partner to Art Deco geometry.

Best for: Doors · Elevator surrounds · Hardware

Stage 01

Consultation & site measure

It starts with the building. SHAPE reviews drawings, photos, and the site itself — openings, structure, existing metal, and how people actually move through the space — then advises on material, finish, and feasibility before anything is priced in detail.

You get: A clear scope, material direction, and next steps by email.
